NB-unif2: When I say “unification”, I mean whatever pulls all the senses together so that a person can talk, cross a road, recognize a friend and answer a text, and it works even when there’s no separate knower in there. Most of my daily life includes that ordinary unification and feels almost like everybody else’s day (well, if they’re happy).
NB-abstract: This article itself is version 2.0 of my old one-page Already Perfect essay. That was already perfect, so why on Earth did I spend weeks rewriting it? Not because of “free will,” but because my boss, Oliver, told me to! 🤪 Put another way, “already perfect without you” means experience is complete before anyone owns it. A tree falls in the woods and makes a sound with nobody there to hear it. A color colors the coloring book with nobody holding the crayon. It sounds abstract, but the next sections explain what I think the experience was showing.
NB-preserve:
The funny part is that the words may have survived surprisingly well. They were transmitted communally for centuries, and separately preserved early collections agree on a great deal despite variants, rearrangements, and later additions. But preserving the puzzle pieces doesn’t preserve the picture on the box.

That creates a practical problem. In DN 3 and MN 56, the Buddha waits until a student’s mind is “ready, pliable, rid of hindrances, elated, and confident” before giving the teaching that opens the Dhamma-eye. What happens when a stage map lets anyone skip to the answer?
HG-B-love: Here is some inner child love. Put your hand over your heart and your other hand on your solar plexus, and say to yourself in a loving way, “Little one, you are not alone. You don’t have to fix this. I’m here now. The adult is listening.” Make sure you are actually talking to your inner child, who is scared to death.
